title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page continues the section of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' that compares an automorphism group M with the loop-equation group γ_{ρ,σ} = Γ_Q^~, Grothendieck's notation for a version of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. The data are as follows.
- Ĝ is (a profinite completion of) the modular group SL2(Z) ≅ Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. Inside it, σ and ρ generate the elliptic stabilizers: σ for the point i, and ρ, with L_ρ ≅ Z/6, for the point -j, j a primitive cube root of unity.
- π = Ker(Ĝ → S_3) is the completed principal congruence subgroup Γ(2), and π ≅ π_0 × μ with π_0 a free profinite group of rank 2 and μ = {±1} the centre.
- M is a group of automorphisms of this structure containing Ĝ. M^! = M(0)·π = Ker(M → S_3), and M^!_0 = M(0)·π_0.
- ε_3 is a sign character with u(ρ) = ρ^{ε_3(u)} for u in N*_ρ.

Previous page. Grothendieck treated the order-4 elliptic element σ. He showed that N*_σ ∩ M^!_0 maps isomorphically onto γ_{ρ,σ} and deduced semi-direct splittings (11). He then recorded N*_ρ (13) and its intersections with Ĝ, G, π and π_0 (14).

This page: the same analysis for the order-6 element ρ, i.e. the elliptic point -j.
- (15) He defines N*_ρ^!_0 = N*_ρ ∩ M^!_0 and N*_ρ^! = N*_ρ ∩ M^!.
- (16) He observes that N*_ρ^!_0 ⊂ Z_ρ = Cent(ρ) = Cent_M(L_ρ). Inside M^!_0 the normalizer of ρ already centralizes it, so the sign ε_3 is trivial there.
- (17) He asserts N*^!_{ρ,0} = Z^!_{ρ,0} =: M'(-j). The name suggests the stabilizer of the elliptic point -j.
- (18) The known homomorphism M → γ_{ρ,σ} induces an isomorphism M'(-j) ≅ γ'_{ρ,σ} = {γ ∈ γ_{ρ,σ} | ε_3(γ) = 1}.
- (19) Consequences. M' and M'^! split as semi-direct products M'(-j)·S^{+} and M'(-j)·π, and M'^!_0 ≃ M'(-j)·π_0. In addition there are direct products Z_ρ^! = N*_ρ^! ≃ M'(-j) × μ and Z*_ρ ≃ M'(-j) × L_ρ. The last two are direct because M'(-j) centralizes L_ρ ⊃ μ.

A crossed-out paragraph compares the two embeddings of γ_{ρ,σ}: via the i-stabilizer (previous page) and via M'(-j) ⊂ N*_ρ. He was apparently checking whether the two sections coincide and abandoned the check.

What it serves. It realizes the GT-type group defined by the loop equations as the stabilizer/centralizer of an elliptic element of order 6 inside automorphisms of profinite SL2(Z) (or Γ(2) ⋊ S_3). This gives splittings of the automorphism groups as GT ⋉ (inner part). The next page then studies the extension by τ' (complex conjugation type), getting a 'quasi-section of multiplicity 2' of M → Γ_Q^~.
errors: Notation inconsistency in (18): the target is written γ'_{ρ,σ} = Γ_Q^~, but it should be the ε_3-kernel, Γ'^~_Q (as on the next page), not Γ_Q^~ itself.

Equation numbers are overwritten (e.g. (15)/(16)/(18) corrected in place). The crossed-out final paragraph is incomplete: the comparison of the two sections (via i and via -j) is not carried out on this page.
The proofs of (16)-(17) are only asserted ('on trouve', 'on montre aussi'), with no argument given here.

ideas.what: The normalizer of the order-6 elliptic element ρ inside the 'pure' part M^!_0 equals its centralizer, M'(-j). This group maps isomorphically onto the ε_3-kernel of the loop-equation group Γ_Q^~.
ideas.modern_name: Identification of (a variant of) \widehat{GT} with a centralizer/stabilizer subgroup in Aut of profinite SL2(Z)/B_3/F_2. Compare the characterization of \widehat{GT} via automorphisms preserving inertia/elliptic classes.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; Lochak–Schneps (1994) on GT and automorphisms of braid groups; Nakamura; Minamide–Nakamura (Out of profinite braid groups)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the GT-tower idea; this specific computation is unsure/unpublished

ideas.what: Semi-direct product splittings M' ≃ M'(-j)·S, M'^! ≃ M'(-j)·π, M'^!_0 ≃ M'(-j)·π_0, and direct products Z_ρ^! ≃ M'(-j)×μ, Z*_ρ ≃ M'(-j)×L_ρ.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting Aut ≅ \widehat{GT}-type group ⋉ Inn for automorphism groups of profinite free/braid/modular groups

ideas.what: Running the same construction at both elliptic points (i via σ, -j via ρ), giving two sections of M → Γ_Q^~, and asking whether they coincide.
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of sections of Aut(\hat{SL_2(Z)}) → \widehat{GT} attached to the two elliptic fixed points

missed.claim: Grothendieck obtains two realizations of the GT-type group as stabilizers of the two elliptic points, M'(i) from σ and M'(-j) from ρ. He starts to compare the resulting two sections of M → Γ_Q^~ and crosses the comparison out. The relation between the two sections (their conjugacy or discrepancy cocycle) is left open on this page.
missed.quote: La correspondance entre M'[0] ≃→ γ_{ρ,σ} ... M'(-j) ⊂ N_ρ^* ≃→ γ_{ρ,σ} ... identique par l'application (18)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The discrepancy between the 'i-section' and the '-j-section' would be a 1-cocycle of \widehat{GT} with values in the modular group. That is close to the f-component of GT elements and to tangential-basepoint path torsors. It is mostly implicit in existing work, but an explicit elliptic-point formulation is not standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The results identify the loop-equation (GT-type) group with the centralizer of an elliptic element in an automorphism group of profinite SL2(Z) and give the associated splittings. They are substantive, but closely parallel later published results (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Minamide–Nakamura). The elliptic-point framing (M'(i), M'(-j)) is a pleasant unpublished detail, not a clear gap in the literature.
transcription_corrections: In (19), line 2 reads M'^! ≃ M'(-j).π (M-prime-shriek), not M''.
In (19), line 1 is likely M' ≃ M'(-j).\mathfrak{S}^{+∧} (hatted/completed S with a + decoration), not \mathfrak{S}_{+1}.
In (19), last line: a crossed-out N is overwritten by Z, giving Z^*_ρ ≃ M'(-j) × L_ρ.
In (16), the first centralizer is Cent_{M(∞)}(ρ) (subscript M(∞)), as in the image.
In (18), γ'_{ρ,σ} is defined as {γ ∈ γ_{ρ,σ} | ε_3(γ) = 1}; the written '= Γ_Q^~' should probably be Γ'^~_Q.
The previous-page transcription 'M(½)' is very likely M'(i), the stabilizer of the elliptic point i for σ, paralleling M'(-j) here.
The final paragraph is entirely struck through. It contains 'M'[0] ≃→ γ_{ρ,σ}', 'M'(-j) ⊂ N_ρ^* ≃→ γ_{ρ,σ}' and 'par l'application (18) M'[0] →'.
